title: DOM + Event Handling
body:
The two halves of every piece of browser [[JavaScript]] in this course, and the pairing
[[JavaScript]] links as one topic.

**The [[DOM]]** is the document as live objects: a [[Tree]] of [[Element Node]]s and
[[Text Node]]s the browser built from the parsed [[HTML]]. **Event handling** is how that tree
tells your code something happened.

Together they give the shape every script here has:

```js
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);

function init() {
	const list = document.querySelector("#list");   // 1. select
	list.addEventListener("click", (e) => {         // 2. attach a handler
		e.target.classList.toggle("done");          // 3. modify
	});
}
```

The `DOMContentLoaded` wrapper is not optional. A script that runs before the parser has built
the tree selects nothing and silently does nothing, which is the single most common reason a
first attempt "doesn't work".

Read [[DOM Algorithm]] for the select-then-modify half and [[Event Handling]] for the other.
Everything else in this group ([[Event Object]], [[Event Propagation]],
[[Event Delegation]], [[DOM Performance]]) is a refinement of one of the two.
